1
00:03:34,520 --> 00:03:40,340
Why, for example, Zenon meant that reality must be an illusion.

2
00:03:41,100 --> 00:03:46,960
To explain this, Aristotle also introduced the concept of "potential".

3
00:03:47,200 --> 00:03:52,300
Built into all matter, there was the potential to become some things.

4
00:03:52,520 --> 00:03:58,860
In an acorns there is the potential to become an oak, however, not to become a dog.

5
00:03:59,340 --> 00:04:04,980
When something has adopted its form, the potential has been updated.

6
00:04:04,980 --> 00:04:07,840
The thing has now become what it can be.

7
00:04:08,880 --> 00:04:13,660
In addition, there is an intention, one purpose, built into everything.

8
00:04:13,800 --> 00:04:21,740
The reason why the acorn strives to become an oak is to secure the species' survival.

9
00:04:22,640 --> 00:04:27,460
Just like his predecessor Plato was Aristotle interested in how to create

10
00:04:55,400 --> 00:05:00,800
Democracy was a matter only for free men, he said.

11
00:05:01,360 --> 00:05:04,620
He assumed that man was a social being,

12
00:05:04,620 --> 00:05:10,280
A political animal that wanted to live with other people.

13
00:05:10,800 --> 00:05:15,240
For this to work, a strict hierarchy was required;

14
00:05:15,500 --> 00:05:21,100
At the bottom of the slave then the children, the wife and at the top man.

15
00:05:21,340 --> 00:05:27,840
This was the natural order and the system would lead to good and safe life.

16
00:05:28,740 --> 00:05:33,680
When the individual has accepted her role, she also becomes happy.

17
00:05:34,080 --> 00:05:41,780
The state's task was to help each family, and, by extension, every individual, to reach this good life.

18
00:05:43,000 --> 00:05:49,880
In the book "The Nikomachian ethics" Aristotle describes its view of ethics and morality.

19
00:05:54,480 --> 00:05:59,420
We are not controlled by instincts but by reason and free will.

20
00:05:59,800 --> 00:06:04,860
We also have no congenital knowledge of right and wrong, good or bad,

21
00:06:04,860 --> 00:06:09,080
Without this, we must learn through training.

22
00:06:09,560 --> 00:06:18,500
We become friendly by performing friendly actions, moderate by performing moderate actions, etc.

23
00:06:19,240 --> 00:06:27,740
By developing and refining their virtues, its positive qualities, we will become better people.

24
00:06:28,260 --> 00:06:32,520
Thus we will automatically act right in different situations

25
00:06:32,520 --> 00:06:37,340
Then good documents originate from good traits.

26
00:06:37,920 --> 00:06:42,880
There are two types of virtues - moral and intellectual.

27
00:06:44,180 --> 00:06:49,040
A good person is also a happy person, Aristotle says.

28
00:06:49,540 --> 00:06:57,820
We all strive to live as social creatures in a society, something that a virtuous person is easy for.

29
00:06:58,400 --> 00:07:04,540
To become virtuous, we must have a balanced attitude to our emotions and desires.

30
00:07:04,700 --> 00:07:12,240
Where this golden middle ground goes varies from person to person, but he gives some simple examples:

31
00:07:12,500 --> 00:07:22,780
Courage is the balance between dumbness and cowardice, generosity is the balance between waste and greed.

32
00:07:23,620 --> 00:07:32,180
The goal of happiness thus goes by learning to become a balanced personality - to be adequate.

33
00:07:33,260 --> 00:07:38,820
As a philosopher, Aristotle was in many ways different from his predecessors.

34
00:07:39,320 --> 00:07:45,620
His research was systematic and based on careful observations of the world

35
00:07:45,620 --> 00:07:51,480
And his philosophy is mostly about what we would call science today.

36
00:07:52,420 --> 00:07:58,280
Thus, there is a clear link between Aristotle and the natural philosophers.

37
00:07:58,680 --> 00:08:05,520
Throughout his life, he immersed himself in research in a way that is unparalleled in Western history,

38
00:08:05,520 --> 00:08:09,040
And his influence is difficult to overestimate.

39
00:08:10,200 --> 00:08:17,160
His geocentric worldview, but the earth in the middle and the planets revolve around this,

40
00:08:17,160 --> 00:08:25,080
was prevailing until the 16th century when Nicolaus Copernicus, Galileo Galilei and Tycho Brahe

41
00:08:25,080 --> 00:08:30,520
Could prove the heliocentric worldview - that it is the sun that is at the center.

42
00:08:31,000 --> 00:08:38,840
This was largely due to the fact that the Catholic Church used his thoughts to construct his worldview.

43
00:08:39,740 --> 00:08:45,400
The Bible's view of creation is also compatible with Aristotle's view

44
00:08:45,400 --> 00:08:50,200
that everything has a built -in purpose, an intention.

45
00:08:51,300 --> 00:08:58,980
To be able to conduct his science, he needed deeper insight into how correct conclusions worked.

46
00:08:59,240 --> 00:09:07,020
The rules for this were not yet known, after which Aristotle created what is today known as logic.

47
00:09:07,500 --> 00:09:14,960
It was not until the end of the 19th century that this logic came to be further developed into what it is today.

48
00:09:16,160 --> 00:09:23,120
Aristotle's engaging with virtually all the sciences of the time, except for mathematics,

49
00:09:23,120 --> 00:09:27,500
And was probably the most learned man of antiquity.

50
00:09:27,960 --> 00:09:36,220
He was the one who mapped many of the sciences we have today - and studies rhetoric or dramaturgy

51
00:09:36,220 --> 00:09:41,900
Is it still Aristotle's virtually unchanged works that you read.

52
00:09:42,960 --> 00:09:47,520
His categorization of plants and animals were prevailing

53
00:09:47,520 --> 00:09:54,780
Until Carl von Linné launched his systematization during the 18th century.

54
00:09:55,220 --> 00:10:02,080
To manage his research, he categorized philosophy in four different categories:

55
00:10:02,080 --> 00:10:06,800
Physics, metaphysics, logic and ethics.

56
00:10:07,100 --> 00:10:13,680
This is a division that we, with some modification, still have today.

1
00:03:34,520 --> 00:03:40,340
varför exempelvis Zenon menade att verkligheten måste vara en illusion.

2
00:03:41,100 --> 00:03:46,960
För att förklara detta införde Aristoteles också begreppet "potential".

3
00:03:47,200 --> 00:03:52,300
Inbyggt i all materia fanns potentialen att bli vissa ting.

4
00:03:52,520 --> 00:03:58,860

5

6
00:04:04,980 --> 00:04:07,840

7
00:04:08,880 --> 00:04:13,660

00:04:13,800 --> 00:04:21,740

00:04:22,640 --> 00:04:27,460
Precis som sin föregångare Platon var Aristoteles intresserad av hur man kunde skapa

00:04:55,400 --> 00:05:00,800

00:05:01,360 --> 00:05:04,620

ett politiskt djur som önskade leva tillsammans med andra människor.

13
00:05:10,800 --> 00:05:15,240
För att detta skulle fungera krävdes en strikt hierarki;

14
00:05:15,500 --> 00:05:21,100
längst ner slaven därefter barnen, hustrun och högst upp mannen.

15
00:05:21,340 --> 00:05:27,840
Detta var den naturliga ordningen och systemet skulle leda till det goda och trygga livet.

16
00:05:28,740 --> 00:05:33,680
När individen accepterat sin roll blir hon också lycklig.

17
00:05:34,080 --> 00:05:41,780
Statens uppgift var att hjälpa varje familj, och i förlängningen varje individ, att nå detta goda liv.

18
00:05:43,000 --> 00:05:49,880
I boken ”Den nikomachiska etiken” beskriver Aristoteles sin syn på etik och moral.

19
00:05:54,480 --> 00:05:59,420
Vi styrs inte av instinkter utan av förnuft och fria vilja.

20
00:05:59,800 --> 00:06:04,860
Vi har heller inga medfödda kunskaper om rätt och fel, bra eller dåligt,

21
00:06:04,860 --> 00:06:09,080
utan detta är någonting måste vi lära oss genom träning.

22
00:06:09,560 --> 00:06:18,500
Vi blir vänliga genom att utföra vänliga handlingar, måttfulla genom att utföra måttfulla handlingar osv.

23
00:06:19,240 --> 00:06:27,740
Genom att utveckla och förädla sina dygder, sina positiva egenskaper, kommer vi att bli bättre människor.

24
00:06:28,260 --> 00:06:32,520
Därmed kommer vi automatiskt att agera rätt i olika situationer

25
00:06:32,520 --> 00:06:37,340
då goda handlingar härstammar från goda karaktärsdrag.

26
00:06:37,920 --> 00:06:42,880
Det finns två typer av dygder – moraliska och intellektuella.

27
00:06:44,180 --> 00:06:49,040
En god människa är också en lycklig människa, menar Aristoteles.

28
00:06:49,540 --> 00:06:57,820
Vi strävar alla efter att leva som sociala varelser i ett samhälle, något som en dygdig person har lätt för.

29
00:06:58,400 --> 00:07:04,540
För att bli dygdig måste vi ha en balanserad hållning till våra känslor och lustar.

30
00:07:04,700 --> 00:07:12,240
Var denna gyllene medelväg går varierar från person till person, men han ger några enkla exempel:

31
00:07:12,500 --> 00:07:22,780
mod är balansen mellan dumdristighet och feghet, givmildhet är balansen mellan slöseri och girighet.

32
00:07:23,620 --> 00:07:32,180
Målet till lycka går alltså genom att lära sig bli en balanserad personlighet –  att vara lagom.

33
00:07:33,260 --> 00:07:38,820
Som filosof var Aristoteles på många sätt annorlunda än sina föregångare.

34
00:07:39,320 --> 00:07:45,620
Hans forskning var systematisk och baserad på noggranna observationer av världen

35
00:07:45,620 --> 00:07:51,480
och hans filosofi handlar mest om vad vi idag skulle kalla naturvetenskap.

36
00:07:52,420 --> 00:07:58,280
Därmed finns en tydlig koppling mellan Aristoteles och naturfilosoferna.

37
00:07:58,680 --> 00:08:05,520
Under hela sitt liv fördjupade han sig i forskning på ett sätt som saknar motstycke i den västerländska historien,

38
00:08:05,520 --> 00:08:09,040
och hans inflytande är svårt att överskatta.

39
00:08:10,200 --> 00:08:17,160
Hans geocentriska världsbild, men jorden i mitten och planeterna kretsande kring denna,

40
00:08:17,160 --> 00:08:25,080
var rådande ända till 1500-talet då Nicolaus Copernicus, Galileo Galilei och Tycho Brahe

41
00:08:25,080 --> 00:08:30,520
kunde bevisa den heliocentriska världsbilden – att det är solen som står i centrum.

42
00:08:31,000 --> 00:08:38,840
Till stor del berodde detta på att den katolska kyrkan använde hans tankar för att konstruera sin världsbild.

43
00:08:39,740 --> 00:08:45,400
Bibelns syn på skapelsen är också förenlig med Aristoteles syn

44
00:08:45,400 --> 00:08:50,200
på att allting har ett inbyggt ändamål, en avsikt.

45
00:08:51,300 --> 00:08:58,980
För att kunna bedriva sin vetenskap behövde han fördjupad insikt i hur korrekta slutledningar fungerade.

46
00:08:59,240 --> 00:09:07,020
Reglerna för detta var ännu inte kända, varpå Aristoteles skapade det som idag är känt som logik.

47
00:09:07,500 --> 00:09:14,960
Det var först i slutet av 1800-talet som denna logik kom att vidareutvecklas till vad den är idag.

48
00:09:16,160 --> 00:09:23,120
Aristoteles sysslande med i stort sett alla dåtidens vetenskaper, undantaget matematik,

49
00:09:23,120 --> 00:09:27,500
och var sannolikt antikens mest lärde man.

50
00:09:27,960 --> 00:09:36,220
Han var den som kartlade många av de vetenskaperna vi har idag – och studerar man retorik eller dramaturgi

51
00:09:36,220 --> 00:09:41,900
är det fortfarande Aristoteles så gott som oförändrade verk som man läser.

52
00:09:42,960 --> 00:09:47,520
Hans kategorisering av växter och djur var rådande

53
00:09:47,520 --> 00:09:54,780
fram till dess att Carl von Linné lanserade sin systematisering under 1700-talet.

54
00:09:55,220 --> 00:10:02,080
För att hantera sin forskning kategoriserade han filosofin i fyra olika kategorier:

55
00:10:02,080 --> 00:10:06,800
Fysik, metafysik, logik och etik.

56
00:10:07,100 --> 00:10:13,680
Detta är en uppdelning som vi, med viss modifikation, har kvar än idag.

1
00:00:21,046 --> 00:00:26,058
enabled him to devote his life to philosophy and searching for knowledge.

00:00:27,001 --> 00:00:32,045
The name Plato is said to be a nickname he received in his youth when he devoted himself to wrestling

00:00:32,054 --> 00:00:36,062
- A name he chose to keep instead of the birth name Aristokles.

00:00:37,098 --> 00:00:41,134
He must have been in his 20s when he was occupied in the circle around Socrates.

00:00:42,034 --> 00:00:47,112
For seven years he studied his teachings, before Socrates finally executed.

6
00:00:48,052 --> 00:00:51,114
At that time Plato was the foremost of the disciples,

00:00:52,014 --> 00:00:56,016
And anyone who would also pass on and develop philosophy.

8
00:00:56,098 --> 00:01:02,154
With Pythagoras as a model, he decided after Socrates' death to start his own philosophy.

9
00:01:03,007 --> 00:01:08,055
The school went under the name Academy (by Akademos, a hero in Greek mythology)

10
00:01:09,002 --> 00:01:13,050
And came to become the role model for today's universities and colleges.

11
00:01:14,026 --> 00:01:21,092
Here, teaching and research was conducted, and in the premises there were lecture rooms, libraries and housing.

12
00:01:22,076 --> 00:01:28,168
The school came to live as an important institution for education for over 900 years before it was closed

13
00:01:29,068 --> 00:01:36,100
By the Byzantine Emperor Justinian I who considered that philosophy was a threat to the Christian faith.

14
00:01:37,002 --> 00:01:40,044
Plato also began writing books on the topic of philosophy.

15
00:02:53,072 --> 00:02:59,074
According to Plato, what we with our senses perceive as reality is not the true reality

16
00:02:59,092 --> 00:03:08,096
Without only a shadow image of it - this when our soul is locked in a body with imperfect knowledge organs.

17
00:03:09,064 --> 00:03:12,096
The idea of ideas can be explained by thinking about a circle.

18
00:03:13,012 --> 00:03:19,006
A drawn circle - thus something that exists in our perceived reality - can never be perfect.

19
00:03:19,006 --> 00:03:23,054
If you look carefully enough, you will always find someone small defect.

20
00:03:24,046 --> 00:03:31,134
What all drawn circles that have ever existed have in common is that they refer to the perfect circle.

21
00:03:32,034 --> 00:03:36,039
But the perfect circle does not exist in our world, it is an abstraction.

22
00:03:37,005 --> 00:03:41,059
The perfect circle - the idea of the circle - is outside time and space.

23
00:03:42,012 --> 00:03:50,012
It is non-material and eternal, and is perfect to its definition.
In addition, there is only one circle idea.

24
00:04:41,054 --> 00:04:45,126
In the same way that the drawn circle has part in the idea of the circle.

25
00:04:46,086 --> 00:04:52,112
Everything that exists in our world is only worse copies of a perfect abstraction.

26
00:04:53,022 --> 00:04:59,108
It is because we humans have the ability to see through reason and thinking the idea of things

27
00:05:00,008 --> 00:05:06,013
which we can also identify and understand them.
This reasoning makes Plato an idealist.

28
00:05:06,074 --> 00:05:13,088
Idealism is a philosophical view where it is believed that reality is basically made up of something non-material

29
00:05:13,088 --> 00:05:15,106
- An idea or consciousness.

30
00:05:16,038 --> 00:05:22,116
This is in contrast to realism or materialism that believes that reality is mainly material.

31
00:05:23,064 --> 00:05:29,148
To explain the idea of idea, Plato Cave Like - a famous Allegori created where he paints a picture

32
00:05:30,048 --> 00:05:34,070
of a couple of prisoners who interpret shadows on the wall as reality.

33
00:05:34,096 --> 00:05:38,110
We are all these prisoners, said Plato, caught in our world of mind.

34
00:05:39,018 --> 00:05:43,019
What we believe is reality is, in fact, only shadows of it.

35
00:05:48,006 --> 00:05:53,062
In a cave, a group of people are imprisoned with their faces facing the inner wall.

36
00:05:54,022 --> 00:06:00,030
They have been sitting there all their lives, and are bound so they have never seen anything other than this particular wall.

37
00:06:01,003 --> 00:06:06,037
Based on the opening of the cave, the sun's rays shine in and throw shadows on the wall in front of the prisoners.

38
00:06:07,003 --> 00:06:10,039
These shadows are the only object that the prisoners have ever seen,

39
00:06:10,066 --> 00:06:12,098
and will for them constitute reality.

40
00:06:14,048 --> 00:06:20,062
It is around this shadow world of the prisoners' lives, and they talk to each other about the things they see.

41
00:06:25,056 --> 00:06:29,108
If any of the prisoners were to detach themselves and escape into the real world

42
00:06:30,044 --> 00:06:33,050
- So he would immediately be dazzled by the sun, as he had never seen before.

43
00:06:35,028 --> 00:06:40,780
When his eyes got used to the light could see that what he previously believed was the act of shadows only,

44
00:06:40,780 --> 00:06:43,840
or worse copies, of something more real.

45
00:06:44,780 --> 00:06:49,900
We are all these prisoners, said Plato, captures in our own world of mind.

46
00:08:59,620 --> 00:09:06,820
Only the most intelligent would be trained to philosophers, an education that went on to the age of 35.

47
00:09:07,000 --> 00:09:12,960
Then followed 15 years of internship before being mature at 50.

48
00:09:13,420 --> 00:09:19,240
He argued here for both class trips and complete gender equality -

49
00:09:19,240 --> 00:09:22,140
Two extremely radical thoughts for their time.

50
00:09:22,380 --> 00:09:29,640
The philosophers were not allowed to have private ownership so as not to be attracted to abuse their power to personal gain.

51
00:09:30,180 --> 00:09:35,260
Everything was owned jointly and one would live in a collective under simple conditions.

52
00:09:35,380 --> 00:09:39,860
The philosopher was not allowed to have any family but the state would arrange big parties

53
00:09:39,860 --> 00:09:44,100
where philosophers of both sexes would meet so that children could be bred.

54
00:09:44,560 --> 00:09:50,540
These children would then be taken from the parents immediately after birth and raised by the state.

55
00:09:50,540 --> 00:09:54,520
No one was told who your child was, so as not to benefit them.

56
00:09:55,460 --> 00:09:59,860
The children would thus consider all of their own age as their siblings

57
00:09:59,860 --> 00:10:04,840
And all in adulthood as their parents - and thus want everyone well.

58
00:10:05,880 --> 00:10:10,460
His purpose with this was to overcome the human selfishness

59
00:10:10,460 --> 00:10:14,280
through a system based on social equality.

60
00:10:14,460 --> 00:10:17,960
The goal was to get a people who would do well in war,

61
00:10:17,960 --> 00:10:22,120
Clearly inspired by the nearby warrior state Sparta.

62
00:10:22,560 --> 00:10:28,780
Plato's political ideas have influenced many of the totalitarian left and right ideologies

63
00:10:28,780 --> 00:10:31,180
which characterized the 20th century.

64
00:10:31,580 --> 00:10:37,640
He must have tried on several occasions to realize his political utopia, but without much success.

1
00:00:21,046 --> 00:00:26,058
möjliggjorde att han kunde ägna sitt liv åt filosofi och sökande efter kunskap.

2
00:00:27,001 --> 00:00:32,045
Namnet Platon sägs vara ett smeknamn han fick i sin ungdom då han ägnade sig åt brottning

3
00:00:32,054 --> 00:00:36,062
– ett namn han valde att behålla istället för födelsenamnet Aristokles.

4
00:00:37,098 --> 00:00:41,134
Han ska ha varit i 20-årsåldern när han upptogs i kretsen kring Sokrates.

5
00:00:42,034 --> 00:00:47,112
Under sju års tid studerade han dennes läror, innan Sokrates slutligen avrättades.

6
00:00:48,052 --> 00:00:51,114
Vid den tidpunkten var Platon den främste av lärjungarna,

7
00:00:52,014 --> 00:00:56,016
och den som också skulle föra vidare och utveckla filosofin.

8
00:00:56,098 --> 00:01:02,154
Med Pythagoras som förebild bestämde han sig efter Sokrates död för att starta en egen filosofiskola.

9
00:01:03,007 --> 00:01:08,055
Skolan gick under namnet Akademin (av Akademos, en hjälte i den grekiska mytologin)

10
00:01:09,002 --> 00:01:13,050
och kom att bli förebilden för dagens universitet och högskolor.

11
00:01:14,026 --> 00:01:21,092
Här bedrevs undervisning och forskning, och i lokalerna fanns både föreläsningssalar, bibliotek och bostäder.

12
00:01:22,076 --> 00:01:28,168
Skolan kom att leva kvar som en viktig institution för utbildning i över 900 år innan den stängdes

13
00:01:29,068 --> 00:01:36,100
av den bysantinske kejsaren Justinianus I som ansåg att filosofin var ett hot mot den kristna tron.

14
00:01:37,002 --> 00:01:40,044
Platon började också skriva böcker om ämnet filosofi.

15
00:02:53,072 --> 00:02:59,074
Enligt Platon är det som vi med våra sinnen uppfattar som verklighet inte den äkta verkligheten

16
00:02:59,092 --> 00:03:08,096
utan endast en skuggbild av den – detta då vår själ är fastlåst i en kropp med ofullkomliga kunskapsorgan.

17
00:03:09,064 --> 00:03:12,096
Idéläran kan förklaras genom att tänka på en cirkel.

18
00:03:13,012 --> 00:03:19,006
En ritad cirkel – alltså något som existerar i vår upplevda verklighet – kan aldrig bli perfekt.

19
00:03:19,006 --> 00:03:23,054
Tittar du tillräckligt noga kommer du alltid att hitta någon liten defekt.

20
00:03:24,046 --> 00:03:31,134
Vad alla ritade cirklar som någonsin har existerat har gemensamt är att de refererar till den perfekta cirkeln.

21
00:03:32,034 --> 00:03:36,039
Men den perfekta cirkeln existerar inte i vår värld, den är en abstraktion.

22
00:03:37,005 --> 00:03:41,059
Den perfekta cirkeln – cirkelns idé – finns utanför tid och rum.

23
00:03:42,012 --> 00:03:50,012
Den är icke-materiell och evig, och är till sin definition perfekt. Därtill finns det bara en cirkeln idé.

24
00:04:41,054 --> 00:04:45,126
på samma sätt som den ritade cirkel har del i cirkelns idé.

25
00:04:46,086 --> 00:04:52,112
Allt som existerar i vår värld är enbart sämre kopior av en perfekt abstraktion.

26
00:04:53,022 --> 00:04:59,108
Det är tack vare att vi människor har förmågan att genom förnuft och tänkande skåda tingens idé

27
00:05:00,008 --> 00:05:06,013
som vi också kan identifiera och förstå dem. Detta resonemang gör Platon till idealist.

28
00:05:06,074 --> 00:05:13,088
Idealism är en filosofisk åskådning där man anser att verkligheten i grunden utgörs av något icke-materiellt

29
00:05:13,088 --> 00:05:15,106
– en idé eller ett medvetande.

30
00:05:16,038 --> 00:05:22,116
Detta till skillnad mot realismen eller materialismen som menar att verkligheten är huvudsakligen materiel.

31
00:05:23,064 --> 00:05:29,148
För att förklara idéläran skapade Platon grottliknelsen – en berömd allegori där han målar upp en bild

32
00:05:30,048 --> 00:05:34,070
av ett par fångar som tolkar skuggor på väggen som verkligheten.

33
00:05:34,096 --> 00:05:38,110
Vi är alla dessa fångar, menade Platon, fångade i vår sinnevärld.

34
00:05:39,018 --> 00:05:43,019
Det vi tror är verkligheten är i själva verket bara skuggor av den.

35
00:05:48,006 --> 00:05:53,062
I en grotta sitter en grupp människor fängslade med ansiktena vända mot den inre väggen.

36
00:05:54,022 --> 00:06:00,030
De har suttit där hela sitt liv, och är bundna så att de aldrig har sett något annat än just denna vägg.

37
00:06:01,003 --> 00:06:06,037
Utifrån grottans öppning skiner solens strålar in och kastar skuggor på väggen framför fångarna.

38
00:06:07,003 --> 00:06:10,039
Dessa skuggor är det enda föremål som fångarna någonsin har sett,

39
00:06:10,066 --> 00:06:12,098
och kommer för dem att utgöra verkligheten.

40
00:06:14,048 --> 00:06:20,062
Det är kring denna skuggvärld fångarnas liv kretsar, och de samtalar med varandra om tingen de ser.

41
00:06:25,056 --> 00:06:29,108
Om någon av fångarna skulle lösgöra sig och fly ut i den verkliga världen

42
00:06:30,044 --> 00:06:33,050
- så skulle han omedelbart bländas av solen, som han aldrig sett förut.

43
00:06:35,028 --> 00:06:40,780
När hans ögon vant sig vid ljuset skulle kan se att det han tidigare trott var vekligheten enbart var skuggor,

44
00:06:40,780 --> 00:06:43,840
eller sämre kopior, av någonting verkligare.

45
00:06:44,780 --> 00:06:49,900
Vi är alla dessa fångar, menade Platon, fångar i vår egen sinnevärld.

46
00:08:59,620 --> 00:09:06,820
Endast de intelligentaste skulle skolas till filosofer, en utbildning som pågick till 35 års ålder.

47
00:09:07,000 --> 00:09:12,960
Därefter följde 15 år av praktik innan man vid 50 var mogen att börja styra.

48
00:09:13,420 --> 00:09:19,240
Han argumenterade här för såväl klassresor som fullständig jämställdhet mellan könen –

49
00:09:19,240 --> 00:09:22,140
två oerhört radikala tankar för sin tid.

50
00:09:22,380 --> 00:09:29,640
Filosoferna fick inte tillåtas ha privat ägande för att inte lockas att missbruka sin makt till personlig vinning.

51
00:09:30,180 --> 00:09:35,260
Allt ägdes gemensamt och man skulle leva i kollektiv under enkla förhållanden.

52
00:09:35,380 --> 00:09:39,860
Filosofen fick inte ha någon familj men staten skulle ordna stora fester

53
00:09:39,860 --> 00:09:44,100
där filosofer av båda könen skulle träffas så att barn kunde avlas.

54
00:09:44,560 --> 00:09:50,540
Dessa barn skulle sedan tas från föräldrarna direkt efter födseln och uppfostras av staten.

55
00:09:50,540 --> 00:09:54,520
Ingen fick veta vilka ens barn var, för att inte kunna gynna dessa.

56
00:09:55,460 --> 00:09:59,860
Barnen skulle därmed betrakta alla i sin egen ålder som sina syskon

57
00:09:59,860 --> 00:10:04,840
och alla i vuxen ålder som deras föräldrar – och därmed vilja allas väl.

58
00:10:05,880 --> 00:10:10,460
Hans syfte med detta var att övervinna den mänskliga själviskheten

59
00:10:10,460 --> 00:10:14,280
genom ett system baserad på social jämställdhet.

60
00:10:14,460 --> 00:10:17,960
Målet var att få fram ett folk som skulle klara sig bra i krig,

61
00:10:17,960 --> 00:10:22,120
tydligt inspirerat av den närbelägna krigarstaten Sparta.

62
00:10:22,560 --> 00:10:28,780
Platons politiska idéer har influerat många av de totalitära vänster- och högerideologier

63
00:10:28,780 --> 00:10:31,180
som kännetecknat 1900-talet.

64
00:10:31,580 --> 00:10:37,640
Han ska vid flera tillfällen ha försökt att förverkliga sin politiska utopi, dock utan större framgång.

1
00:01:56,520 --> 00:01:58,820
Anyone who believed to know the answer was challenged

2
00:01:58,940 --> 00:02:04,140
And Socrates submitted the answer a review by asking a number of follow -up questions.

3
00:02:04,580 --> 00:02:08,100
Almost always emerged the shortcomings in the original response

4
00:02:08,100 --> 00:02:12,240
Then the interlocutor revised the reasoning and tried again.

5
00:02:12,760 --> 00:02:19,460
Socratic thinking became famous and it revealed ignorance in people with alleged knowledge.

6
00:02:20,020 --> 00:02:26,060
Although Socrates herself rarely gave any final answers (and in that case it would have been included in his method

7
00:02:26,060 --> 00:02:33,320
To emphasize that each such response would also be subjected to review) he stimulated an interest in philosophy.

8
00:02:33,580 --> 00:02:37,920
He taught people to question everything, which would also be his ruin.

9
00:02:38,220 --> 00:02:43,080
In the end, he was arrested by the authorities who are tired of being constantly being questioned,

10
00:02:43,080 --> 00:02:44,760
And he was sentenced to death.

11
00:02:45,060 --> 00:02:50,280
Although his friends and students offered help in fleeing, Socrates opposed this

12
00:02:50,280 --> 00:02:54,560
And talked about how citizens must obey the laws and the authorities' decisions.

13
00:03:07,560 --> 00:03:10,620
There are lots of rumors and claims about Socrates,

14
00:03:10,640 --> 00:03:14,040
Among other things, he is said to have been small, thick and unusually ugly.

15
00:03:14,200 --> 00:03:19,080
According to information he was married to Xantippa - a very quarrelsome and angry woman,

16
00:03:19,180 --> 00:03:22,680
But also the only one who could defeat Socrates in a discussion.

17
00:03:23,120 --> 00:03:27,900
He is alleged to have also been virtually insensitive to cold and physical exertion,

18
00:03:28,080 --> 00:03:32,920
And it is said that he could stand pondering for hours, completely unaware of the outside world.

19
00:03:33,320 --> 00:03:40,620
Often he spoke to his inner voice, his "daimon", when he doubted that a way to act really the right thing.

20
00:03:41,040 --> 00:03:46,540
A major problem when it comes to our knowledge of Socrates is that he never wrote anything.

21
00:03:46,740 --> 00:03:51,480
Most of what we know about him comes from his students, mainly Plato.

22
00:03:51,820 --> 00:03:55,600
But what is really reproduced by Socrates thoughts in these writings

23
00:03:55,660 --> 00:04:00,700
And what in turn is Plato's own doctrine is something that is constantly being discussed.

24
00:04:01,160 --> 00:04:05,440
In summary, Socrates has had a huge influence on philosophy.

25
00:04:05,800 --> 00:04:12,700
Not only did he define many of the issues that philosophy is still engaged in today, such as moral philosophy,

26
00:04:12,820 --> 00:04:20,180
His dialectical method and emphasis on critical thinking have permeated philosophy since the days of ancient times.

1
00:01:56,520 --> 00:01:58,820
Den som trodde sig veta svaret utmanades

2
00:01:58,940 --> 00:02:04,140
och Sokrates underkastade svaret en granskning genom att ställa en rad följdfrågor.

3
00:02:04,580 --> 00:02:08,100
Nästan alltid framkom det brister i det ursprungliga svaret

4
00:02:08,100 --> 00:02:12,240
varpå samtalspartnern reviderade resonemanget och försökte igen.

5
00:02:12,760 --> 00:02:19,460
Det sokratiska tänkandet blev berömt och det avslöjade okunnighet hos personer med påstådd kunskap.

6
00:02:20,020 --> 00:02:26,060
Även om Sokrates själv sällan gav några slutgiltiga svar (och det skulle i så fall ha ingått i hans metod

7
00:02:26,060 --> 00:02:33,320
att betona att varje sådant svar också skulle utsättas för granskning) så stimulerade han ett intresse för filosofi.

8
00:02:33,580 --> 00:02:37,920
Han lärde människor att ifrågasätta allt, något som också skulle bli hans fördärv.

9
00:02:38,220 --> 00:02:43,080
Till slut arresterades han av myndigheterna som tröttnat på att hela tiden bli ifrågasatta,

10
00:02:43,080 --> 00:02:44,760
och han dömdes till döden.

11
00:02:45,060 --> 00:02:50,280
Trots att hans vänner och elever erbjöd hjälp med att fly motsatte sig Sokrates detta

12
00:02:50,280 --> 00:02:54,560
och talade om hur medborgarna måste lyda lagarna och myndigheternas beslut.

13
00:03:07,560 --> 00:03:10,620
Det finns massor med rykten och påståenden om Sokrates,

14
00:03:10,640 --> 00:03:14,040
bland annat sägs han ha varit liten, tjock och ovanligt ful.

15
00:03:14,200 --> 00:03:19,080
Enligt uppgifter var han gift med Xantippa - en mycket grälsjuk och argsint kvinna,

16
00:03:19,180 --> 00:03:22,680
men också den enda som kunde besegrade Sokrates i en diskussion.

17
00:03:23,120 --> 00:03:27,900
Han påstås även ha varit i det närmaste okänslig för kyla och fysisk ansträngning,

18
00:03:28,080 --> 00:03:32,920
och det sägs att han kunde stå grubblandes i timtal, helt omedveten om omvärlden.

19
00:03:33,320 --> 00:03:40,620
Ofta talade han till sin inre röst, sin "daimon", när han tvivlade på att ett sätt att handla verkligen det rätta.

20
00:03:41,040 --> 00:03:46,540
Ett stort problem när det gäller vår kunskap om Sokrates är att han aldrig skrev någonting.

21
00:03:46,740 --> 00:03:51,480
Det mesta av det vi känner till om honom kommer från hans elever, huvudsakligen Platon.

22
00:03:51,820 --> 00:03:55,600
Men vad som verkligen återgivits av Sokrates tankar i dessa skrifter

23
00:03:55,660 --> 00:04:00,700
och vad som i sin tur är Platons egen lära är något som ständigt diskuteras.

24
00:04:01,160 --> 00:04:05,440
Sammanfattningsvis har Sokrates haft ett enormt inflytande på filosofin.

25
00:04:05,800 --> 00:04:12,700
Inte nog med att han definierade många av de frågor som filosofin än i dag ägnar sig åt, t ex moralfilosofi,

26
00:04:12,820 --> 00:04:20,180
hans dialektiska metod och betoning på kritiskt tänkande har genomsyrat filosofin sedan antikens dagar.

and colonies along large parts of the Mediterranean.

Without the help of reason to understand the world.

began to refer to human decisions and natural circumstances

with Athens as the dominant city state.

14

Here, culture and free debate flourished in a way that was unparalleled in the ancient world.

15

To this cultural center, thinkers sought from all of the Greek civilization

And now the city ended up in the philosophical eye -catching.

17

(ofta med visst folkligt stöd) istället för att ha ärvt den.

3
00:00:28,620 --> 00:00:35,820
Dåtidens Grekland var också betydligt större än idag och inkluderade bland annat delar av nuvarande Turkiet

4
00:00:35,920 --> 00:00:39,180
och kolonier längs stora delar av Medelhavet.

5
00:00:40,120 --> 00:00:46,260
Vid denna tidpunkt framträdde ett antal tänkare som började ifrågasätta de rådande sanningarna.

6
00:00:46,620 --> 00:00:50,420
De nöjde sig inte längre med att lita på myter och gudasagor

7
00:00:50,700 --> 00:00:54,420
utan försökte med förnuftets hjälp att förstå sig på världen.

8
00:00:55,180 --> 00:01:01,400
Tidigare hade kunskap om myterna varit det som gav folket mening och vägledning i livet.

9
00:01:02,020 --> 00:01:10,160
Torka och sjukdomar, krig och olycka, födelse och död -- allt berodde enligt tron på gudarnas makt och inflytande.

10
00:03:38,260 --> 00:03:42,420
började hänvisa till mänskliga beslut och naturliga omständigheter

11
00:03:42,780 --> 00:03:47,200
- det var inte längre gudarna som avgjorde människans öde, det var hon själv.

12
00:03:47,960 --> 00:03:52,520
Så småningom utvecklades Grekland till en ekonomisk och militär stormakt

13
00:03:52,620 --> 00:03:55,640
med Aten som den dominerande stadsstaten.

14
00:03:56,320 --> 00:04:01,840
Här blomstrade kultur och fri debatt på ett sätt som saknade motstycke i den antika världen.

15
00:04:02,500 --> 00:04:07,460
Till detta kulturella centrum sökte sig tänkare från hela den grekiska civilisationen
